An airplane to be eligible for night operation shall have installed an anti-collision light system. Such system shall consist of one or more approved anticollision lights so located that the emitted light will not be detrimental to the crew's vision and will not detract from the conspicuity of the position lights. The system shall comply with the provisions of paragraphs (a) through (d) of this section.
(a) Field of coverage. The system shall consist of such lights as will afford coverage of all vital areas around the airplane with due consideration to the physical configuration and the flight characteristics of theoftPlane. In any case, the field of coverage shall extend in 411 directions within 36° above and 30° below the horizontal plane of the airplane, except that a solid angle or angles of obstructed visibility totaling not more than .03 steradians shall be pérmigsible within a solid angle equal to .15 steradians centered about the longitudinal axie in thé rearward direction.
(b) Flashing characteristics. The arrangement of the system, i.e., mmber of light sources beam width, speed of rotation, etc., shall be auch as to give an effective flash freqiency of not less than 40 and not more than 100 cycles per minute. The effective flash frequency shall be the frequency at which the airplane's complete anti-collision light system is observed fram a distance, aid shall apply to all sectors of light including the overlaps which might exist when the system consists of more than one light source. In overlaps, flash frequencies higher than 100 cycles per mimite shall be permissible, except that they shall not be higher than 180 cycles per minute.
(c) Color. The color of the anti-collision lights shall be aviation red in accordatice with the specifications of § 3.703 (a).
